title: 🌍 Customs, Duties and Taxes: What Should I Know?
content:
If you are shipping products from China to another country, your parcel may need to go through customs clearance.

This guide explains what customs clearance means, what duties and taxes are, who may need to pay them, and what you should know before submitting your parcel for international shipping.


🌟 Simple overview

When your parcel enters your destination country, it may be checked by local customs.

Customs may review:

  • What items are inside the parcel
  • The declared value
  • The quantity of items
  • The purpose of the shipment
  • The recipient information
  • Whether the items are allowed to be imported
  • Whether duties or taxes need to be paid

Customs rules are different in each country. Please check your local import rules before shipping.


1. 🛃 What is customs clearance?

Customs clearance is the process where your destination country checks and approves an international parcel before it can be delivered.

During customs clearance, the local customs authority may:

  • Inspect the parcel
  • Review the declaration information
  • Check whether the item is restricted
  • Calculate import duties or taxes
  • Ask the recipient to provide extra documents
  • Release, delay, return, or reject the parcel

Customs clearance is a normal part of international shipping.


2. 💰 What are duties and taxes?

Duties and taxes are fees charged by your destination country when goods are imported.

They may include:

  • Customs duty
  • Import tax
  • VAT
  • GST
  • Sales tax
  • Consumption tax
  • Customs handling fee
  • Local courier processing fee

These fees are usually decided by the destination country’s customs authority or local delivery company.

They are not always included in the international shipping fee.


3. 📦 Does international shipping fee include taxes?

Not always.

Some shipping methods may include tax handling, while others do not.

Before choosing a shipping method, please check whether it is:

  • Tax-included
  • Tax-not-included
  • DDP
  • DDU
  • DAP
  • Delivered by postal service
  • Delivered by commercial express courier

If the shipping method does not include taxes, you may need to pay duties or taxes when the parcel arrives in your country.


4. ✅ What does DDP mean?

DDP usually means “Delivered Duty Paid.”

With a DDP shipping method, tax and customs handling may be included in the shipping service.

This means the sender or logistics provider usually handles import duty and tax-related arrangements before delivery.

However, please note:

  • DDP rules may vary by route
  • Some item categories may not be supported
  • Some remote areas may have extra fees
  • Customs may still inspect the parcel
  • Extra documents may still be required in special cases

Please always check the shipping method details before choosing a DDP route.


5. ⚠️ What do DDU and DAP mean?

DDU and DAP usually mean that duties and taxes are not included in the shipping fee.

If your parcel is taxed by customs, the recipient may need to pay the tax before delivery.

In this case, the local courier or customs authority may contact you by:

  • Email
  • SMS
  • Phone call
  • Postal notice
  • Online payment link
  • Delivery notice

If you do not pay the required tax or provide the required documents in time, the parcel may be delayed, returned, or disposed of according to local rules.


6. 🧾 What is declared value?

Declared value is the value of the goods submitted to customs for clearance.

It helps customs understand the estimated value of the parcel.

Declared value may affect:

  • Whether the parcel is taxed
  • The amount of duties or taxes
  • Customs inspection risk
  • Whether extra documents are required
  • Whether the parcel is treated as personal or commercial goods

Please make sure declaration information is reasonable and accurate.


7. 🚫 Can I declare a very low value to avoid taxes?

We do not recommend false declaration.

Incorrect or unreasonable declaration may cause:

  • Customs delay
  • Extra document requests
  • Parcel return
  • Parcel confiscation
  • Tax reassessment
  • Penalties
  • Failed compensation claims
  • Account restrictions

Customs decisions are made by the destination country. A low declared value does not guarantee that taxes will be avoided.

Please follow the laws and customs rules of your country.


8. 📋 What information may customs require?

Depending on your country and the shipping method, customs or the local courier may ask for additional information.

They may request:

  • Recipient full name
  • Phone number
  • Tax ID
  • ID number
  • Passport number
  • Business registration number
  • Product invoice
  • Payment proof
  • Product description
  • Product usage explanation
  • Import permit, if required

Please provide the requested information as soon as possible to avoid delays.


9. ⏳ Why is my parcel delayed at customs?

Customs delays may happen for many reasons.

Common reasons include:

  • Customs inspection
  • Incomplete declaration information
  • Incorrect recipient information
  • Restricted item category
  • High declared value
  • Large quantity of similar items
  • Missing tax ID or ID number
  • Peak season customs backlog
  • Local holidays
  • Courier processing delay
  • Customs requesting extra documents

Customs processing time is not fully controlled by our website or the logistics provider.


10. 📦 Personal use vs. commercial use

Customs may treat parcels differently depending on whether they appear to be for personal use or commercial use.

A parcel may be considered commercial if it contains:

  • Many identical items
  • Large quantities
  • High total value
  • Products for resale
  • Business-related goods

Commercial parcels may require additional customs documents, higher taxes, or formal import procedures.

If you are shipping goods for business use or resale, please confirm your local import requirements before submitting the parcel.


11. 🧴 Restricted items and customs risk

Some products may have higher customs risk.

Examples include:

  • Food
  • Medicine
  • Supplements
  • Cosmetics
  • Liquids
  • Powders
  • Batteries
  • Electronics
  • Branded goods
  • Replica products
  • Animal or plant products
  • Large quantities of the same item

Even if a product can be shipped, it may still be inspected, taxed, delayed, rejected, or returned by customs.

Please check item restrictions before purchasing or shipping.


12. 🔄 What happens if customs rejects my parcel?

If customs rejects a parcel, possible results may include:

  • The parcel is returned to the sender
  • The parcel is held for further review
  • The parcel is destroyed according to local rules
  • The recipient must provide extra documents
  • The recipient must pay duties, taxes, or penalties
  • The logistics provider charges return or handling fees

The final result depends on the destination country’s customs rules and logistics provider policy.

If your parcel is rejected or delayed, please contact customer service and provide the customs notice or logistics message.


13. 💳 Who pays customs duties and taxes?

In most cases, customs duties and import taxes are paid by the recipient.

However, this depends on the shipping method.

  • If you choose a tax-included or DDP route, tax handling may already be included.
  • If you choose a tax-not-included, DDU, or DAP route, the recipient may need to pay taxes after the parcel arrives.
  • If customs charges extra fees due to special inspection or incorrect information, the recipient may need to handle them.

Please read the shipping method description carefully before payment.


14. 🧠 How to reduce customs problems

To reduce customs risks, we recommend:

  • Choose a suitable shipping method
  • Avoid prohibited or high-risk items
  • Provide accurate recipient information
  • Use a reasonable declared value
  • Avoid shipping too many identical items in one parcel
  • Prepare tax ID or ID information if your country requires it
  • Respond quickly if customs or the courier contacts you
  • Contact customer service before shipping sensitive items

Please note that these steps may reduce risk, but they cannot guarantee that customs will not inspect or tax your parcel.


Example 1: Tax-not-included route

You choose a normal shipping method that does not include taxes.

The parcel arrives in your country.

Local customs reviews the parcel and charges import tax.

The local courier contacts you and asks you to pay the tax before delivery.

After you pay, the parcel continues to the final delivery address.


Example 2: Tax-included route

You choose a tax-included shipping method.

The tax handling is included in the shipping service under the route rules.

In most normal cases, you do not need to pay additional import tax when the parcel arrives.

However, customs may still inspect the parcel or ask for documents in special cases.


Example 3: Customs needs more information

Your parcel arrives in your country, but customs needs more information.

The courier asks you to provide your tax ID and payment proof.

You provide the required information.

After customs approves the parcel, it is released for local delivery.


Important notes

  • Customs rules are different in each country.
  • International shipping fee does not always include duties or taxes.
  • DDP or tax-included routes may include tax handling, but restrictions still apply.
  • DDU or DAP routes may require the recipient to pay taxes after arrival.
  • Declared value should be reasonable and accurate.
  • False declaration may cause delays, returns, penalties, or confiscation.
  • Customs clearance time is not fully controlled by our website.
  • The recipient is responsible for cooperating with customs when required.
  • Restricted items may have higher customs risk.
  • Please check local import rules before shipping special items.


Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: Will I always need to pay customs duties?

No. Whether duties or taxes are charged depends on your country, parcel value, item type, shipping method, and customs decision.

Q2: Are customs duties included in the international shipping fee?

Not always. Some routes include tax handling, while others do not. Please check the shipping method description before payment.

Q3: What is the difference between DDP and DDU?

DDP usually means duties and tax handling are included in the shipping service. DDU usually means duties and taxes are not included, and the recipient may need to pay them after the parcel arrives.

Q4: Can you guarantee that my parcel will not be taxed?

No. Customs decisions are made by the destination country. We cannot guarantee that a parcel will not be taxed or inspected.

Q5: Why does customs ask me for documents?

Customs may need to verify the recipient, product type, value, or import purpose. Please provide the requested documents as soon as possible.

Q6: What if I refuse to pay customs tax?

If taxes are required and not paid, the parcel may be delayed, returned, destroyed, or handled according to local customs rules. Extra fees may apply.

Q7: Can I change the declared value?

Declaration rules depend on the shipping method and customs requirements. The declared value should be reasonable and accurate. Please contact customer service before submitting your parcel if you have questions.


Need help?

If you are not sure about customs, duties, taxes, or declaration rules, please contact our customer service team before submitting your parcel.

To help us assist you faster, please provide:

  • Your destination country
  • Product link or item name
  • Item quantity
  • Estimated item value
  • Preferred shipping method
  • Whether the item is for personal or business use
  • Any customs notice or courier message, if already received

We will help you understand the available shipping options and possible customs considerations.
